**Series book (absolute method) — continuity with the published put/call series**

- **Universe: the 8 Pass-B mega-caps (IWM, GLD, TLT, AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN).** Every ratio in this section describes THOSE 8 names and nothing else —
- it is not the relative screen's population. The legacy method, unchanged: per-underlying top-10 by volume, 4 earliest listed expiries, V/OI ≥ 1.0, volume ≥ 200, DTE ≤ 60.
- **Bias tag: CALL** (put/call 0.64), thresholds < 0.85 → CALL, > 1.2 → PUT, else MIXED.

**Wide book — the same method over the relative screen's universe**

- **Universe: the 60-name relative-screen universe** (the top 60 US names by cash volume plus the 8 routine names).
- This is the SAME legacy absolute method as the series book above —
- per-underlying top-10 by volume, 4 earliest listed expiries, V/OI ≥ 1.0, volume ≥ 200, DTE ≤ 60 — applied to the wide population.
- Only the POPULATION differs from the series book, so the two rows are comparable:
- the series book answers "what did the 8 mega-caps do", the wide book answers "what did the market's most-traded 60 names do".
- It does NOT replace the series book, which carries the published put/call series since 2026-10-16.

- **Slice**: All kept (legacy method, wide universe) · **Universe**: 60 names · **Rows**: 299 · **Call volume**: 4,687,527 (+3 more column(s) in the artifact table)

- **Reading the two books together:** series book (the 8 mega-caps) put/call 0.64 → **CALL**; wide book (the 60 most-traded names) put/call 0.61 → **CALL**.
- A reader who sees only one of these numbers is reading one population and will assume it is the market.

**Caveats**

- **The own-history baseline is a 4-venue number and it lags the live session.** Cboe's historical service covers only the Cboe-operated venues (CBOE, BATS, C2, EDGX) while the chain covers every US venue, so the *ratio* is internally consistent (4-venue vs 4-venue) but the absolute volumes are a different universe from the chain column beside them.
- The service also publishes the current session with a lag, so the baseline here is measured on 2026/11/06 while the contract screen is 2026-11-09 —
- one session apart, labelled on every row.
- **The peer median is over strikes with volume >= 50.** Including the long tail of near-dead strikes would inflate every peer ratio; excluding them would suppress it.
- The group median and group size are published on every row so the ratio is auditable.
- **A ratio on a trivial number is still a trivial number.** A high own-history ratio can rest on a few hundred contracts —
- always read the ratio next to the volume.
- **The composite is an ensemble, not a statistic.** Every component is published per row so the ranking can be re-derived or re-weighted; a single-metric view is a sort away.
- **V/OI is an upper bound on a gap day.** Cboe's open interest is the prior session's settled OI while the volume is today's session, so V/OI is inflated by construction when fresh positions open all session.
- The OI >= 50 slice in the series book exists for this reason.
- **0DTE IV is degenerate after the close** and the 0DTE rows in the all-expiries table inherit it; the multi-day table is the interpretable one.
- **Deep-ITM rows are often closing trades, not bets** — a large theoretical value with V/OI near 1 and a big open interest is the signature.
- **The universe is the most-traded names, not the whole market** — a relative screen over a fixed universe can only find anomalies inside it.
- **Three populations, three named books.** The relative screen covers the 60-name relative-screen universe, the series book the 8 Pass-B mega-caps, and Pass A the published watchlist.
- Their ratios describe different populations and are not interchangeable — which is why every ratio in this file names its universe.
